note: Operator-implemented capture purpose and retention schedule for DC00 (migration 0052 + packages/learning/policy.js). The thirteen other classes below are the already-demonstrated staging canary evidence recorded at 3e51ba0c, whose 0044-0051 bytes are identical to this branch. A green result is NOT legal approval, NOT production authorization and NOT training authorization: productionAuthorized and trainingAuthorized stay false.

privacyPurpose.artifact: Owner-approved capture purpose, implemented as a one-time per-actor choice (migration 0052: learning.consent + learning.record_consent/withdraw_research). Necessary operational processing and optional research are SEPARATE columns; optional_research has no default, and DB CHECK consent_affirmative_required_ck refuses an affirmative without an explicit consent_version, an affirmative granted_at AND age_band=adult (CAPTURE_CONSENT_ADULT_ONLY). Absence of a row is NOT consent (research_eligible returns false). One choice is stored and synchronised; there is no per-match prompt. Withdrawal stops the permission, records withdrawn_at and raises the privacy epoch via learning.suppress(), revoking every open export. Proven on real PostgreSQL16 by tests/v52-consent-retention.test.js; 0052 applied on top of 0051 (52/52) and re-applied with 0 pending.

retention.artifact: Owner-delegated schedule implemented as DATA (learning.retention_schedule, 10 rows with window, basis, neverPastSource, review interval, legal-review flag) and swept by packages/learning/policy.js runRetention(db,{kind}) on a schedule: adult consented captures 730d with an annual necessity review; working exports 90d and never past source expiry; raw ad analytics 90d; pending client-upload spool 7d bounded by min(window, source expiry); ordinary encrypted backups 35d only once safe pruning is verified. Purchases, fraud, operations and security keep separate rows with NO window until their legal review; youth research is a separate lawful protocol that can never carry an adult window. Withdrawal and applicable law override every maximum: learning.expiry_bound() enforces LEAST(scheduled,source), a withdrawal raises the epoch, and the erasure sweep nulls the archived payload. Proven on real PostgreSQL16 by tests/v52-consent-retention.test.js.

encryptedStorage.artifact: Encrypted archive round trip. STAGING (capture_exporter exact role): shipped `export` wrote run b2ef8e0a-efbd-4dc0-a12f-40c42b17f40e (616 B, plainSha256 4329b2839688ef5f..., cipherSha256 e89cd9b231b07454...); the offline reader re-authenticated it record by record (readBack.ok=true). It scanned 15 sealed captures and excluded all 15 on population grounds (staging actors are unclassified, so the exporter REFUSES them - correct, not an omission). The record-level path ran where games DO flow, on the lab: run b501f860-1498-478d-b409-b7bbb5a22ce7, 115 records, 2 games, readBack.ok=true, no time leak. MXOCAP1 = AES-256-GCM, per-file HKDF-SHA256 key from a 256-bit 0600 key file. Evidence: .artifacts/dc00/staging-canary-clean.json steps.export; lab-controls.json steps.exportLineage.

deletionSweep.artifact: learning.erase(n) runs on schedule in the staging maintenance chain as the capture_privacy role (one real systemd run: {"erased":0} with 15 sealed untouched - an honest idempotent no-op, since nothing was eligible). The destructive half was demonstrated where a deletion actually existed: on the lab the same shipped `erase` reported undefined and the participant's sealed capture became suppressed with payload NULL and 0 subjects. The sweep also invalidates exports and bumps the privacy epoch whenever it removes anything. Evidence: journalctl -u mega-xo-v51-capture-maintenance.service, .artifacts/dc00/staging-controls.json steps.eraseNoOp, .artifacts/dc00/lab-controls.json steps.authenticatedDeletion. GAP: the staging host's erase cadence has never been exercised against a real deletion on staging, because no staging deletion exists.

exportPurge.artifact: On real staging: learning.revoke_export(b2ef8e0a-efbd-4dc0-a12f-40c42b17f40e) set the run to state=revoked; an operator-confirmed `purge-exports` (capture_exporter role, executed in the same authenticated operator session as the run above) reported {"purged":1} and the ciphertext file b2ef8e0a-efbd-4dc0-a12f-40c42b17f40e.mxocap no longer exists (fileExistsAfterPurge=false); the subsequent scheduled pass reported {"purged":0}. The reader fence was also proven: readDataset() aborts with CAPTURE_EXPORT_REVOKED the moment the run is revoked or the epoch moves - observed for real in the lab when the caller passed a pre-erasure epoch, and again after revocation. Evidence: .artifacts/dc00/staging-canary-clean.json steps.exportPurge, .artifacts/dc00/staging-controls.json steps.purgeExportsIdempotent, .artifacts/dc00/lab-controls.json steps.exportLineage.

restoreJournal.artifact: The real recovery contract was executed, not described. An encrypted privacy journal was written (3 records, epoch 2, suppressions 1, erasures 1, cipherSha256 92fb66751e67e63e...) and then replayed by the shipped `restore-journal` into a SECOND, independently created isolated database that had collection DISABLED, with CAPTURE_ISOLATED_RESTORE=1, the journal digest pinned and the required epoch supplied: {"sourceEpoch":2,"targetEpoch":2,"entries":2,"enabled":false}. The replay re-applied the suppression and the erasure tombstone, ran the erasure sweep to exhaustion, and left the target with enabled=false at epoch 2, so a restored backup can never resume collecting over replayed deletions. The shipped CLI additionally refuses this mode unless the target is a test/nonserving target (CAPTURE_RESTORE_ISOLATION_REQUIRED). Evidence: .artifacts/dc00/lab-controls.json steps.restoreJournal.

postgresRestart.artifact: The PostgreSQL cluster hosting the captures was really stopped and restarted (pg_ctl -D $TMPDIR/v5-p05lab-pg-97397-7InCYL -m fast restart -w) while a capture was still pending. Before the restart: {"captures":8,"pending":1}. After: {"captures":8,"pending":1,"sealed":5,"ready":1} - the row count and the pending obligation both survived, and the connection was healthy. The shipped one-shot worker then reclaimed and sealed it: {"disabled":false,"claimed":1,"sealed":1,"quarantined":0,"suppressed":0,"excluded":0,"retry":0,"stale":0,"errors":{}}; metrics {"purged":0,"sealed":6,"pending":0,"excluded":1,"suppressed":1,"quarantined":0,"expiredUnpurged":0,"oldestPendingSeconds":0}. Nothing was lost and nothing was duplicated. Evidence: .artifacts/dc00/lab-controls.json steps.postgresRestart. GAP: this proves the collector's Postgres durability, NOT a Neon compute-suspend/resume event on staging - no staging restart was performed.

redisLoss.artifact: Real Core games were settled with NO ephemera (Redis) adapter present at all, so every publishMatchHint call returns {published:false,available:false,conservative:true} and no match notification can be delivered. A real queue match (offer, both accepts, two moves, resignation) settled anyway; the durable capture obligation appeared with pending 0 -> 1 because it is written by the deferred Postgres constraint trigger INSIDE the settlement transaction, and the shipped worker then sealed it: {"disabled":false,"claimed":1,"sealed":1,"quarantined":0,"suppressed":0,"excluded":0,"retry":0,"stale":0,"errors":{}}; final disposition {"state":"sealed"}. Redis absence can delay a hint, but it cannot lose an intent. Evidence: .artifacts/dc00/lab-controls.json steps.redisLoss. GAP: no Upstash staging Redis outage was induced; Upstash was not used by the capture path at all.

latencyAndQuota.artifact: Bounded paired measurement over 24 real Core games (+2 warmup) with learning.policy.enabled toggled per game, because the capture cost lands on the deferred settlement trigger. move ms ON n=39 p50 17.557 / p95 20.768 vs OFF p50 17.684 / p95 19.475 (delta p50 -0.127, p95 1.293); settlement ms ON p50 18.193 / p95 20.118 vs OFF p50 18.119 / p95 19.068 (delta p50 0.074, p95 1.05). Across repeated runs the sign of both deltas flips, so the honest reading is "inside loopback noise at this sample size". Quota inputs from real sealed payloads: raw 1419/1421/5493 bytes and gzip 594/598/1200 bytes per game (min/p50/max). SCOPE LIMIT: laptop loopback with a warm local PG16; a 0.25-CU Neon staging path and a real player cohort are NOT represented, so no staging latency SLA and no alert threshold is claimed here. Evidence: .artifacts/dc00/lab-controls.json steps.latencyAndQuota.

absent.noticeAndControllerSignoff: The public in-product notice naming this specific use and the privacy-controller sign-off remain owed (legal). The capture-specific opt-out/withdrawal control is implemented server-side; its client surface belongs to the account/UI lane and is not claimed here.
